block_node.block_desc:
This block models a counterbalance valve in an thermal liquid network that is typically used to hold suspended loads. Ports L, B, and P are thermal liquid conserving ports associated with the load pressure, back pressure, and pilot pressure, respectively. The valve is normally closed to prevent flow between ports L and B. When the set pressure differential is reached, the valve opens to permit liquid flow. Pressure at ports P and L act to open the valve, while pressure at port B acts to close the valve. A separate check valve connected across ports B and L permits a parallel flow path from port B to port L but not in the reverse direction. There is no flow through the pilot pressure port P.
For the Tabulated data - Volumetric flow rate vs. pressure setting, the relief stage reference pressure differential vector and reference volumetric flow rate vector assume that both the pilot pressure port P and back pressure port B are set to standard atmospheric pressure. The set pressure differential shifts the reference curve so relief valve cracking occurs when the control pressure differential equals the set pressure differential.

block_node.block_desc: Double-click the block to bring up the contour plot. Click the 'Select fluid properties' button to choose a Two-Phase Fluid Properties (2P) or Two-Phase Fluid Predefined Properties (2P) block in the model and update the temperature contours. The Simulink inputs p and h provide the pressure-enthalpy coordinates of each point in the thermodynamic cycle. The number of cycle points is equal to the number of elements in p and h.
